-- Pediatric obesity cohort: any obesity descendant condition diagnosed at age < 18
WITH obesity_concepts AS (
  SELECT ca.descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (433736, 40481140) -- Obesity (disorder), Childhood obesity
),
ped_obese AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT co.person_id
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN obesity_concepts oc ON co.condition_concept_id = oc.concept_id
  JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = co.person_id
  WHERE DATEDIFF(YEAR, DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth, ISNULL(p.month_of_birth,6), ISNULL(p.day_of_birth,15)), co.condition_start_date) < 18
    AND DATEDIFF(YEAR, DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth, ISNULL(p.month_of_birth,6), ISNULL(p.day_of_birth,15)), co.condition_start_date) >= 2
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_pediatric_obese_patients FROM ped_obese;

cat AS (
  SELECT 'Anxiety disorders' AS category, ca.descendant_concept_id AS concept_id FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 442077

  UNION SELECT 'Eating disorders', ca.descendant_concept_id FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 439002

pat AS (

## Mental health co-occurrence in children with obesity

**Cohort:** 39,031 patients with an obesity diagnosis recorded at ages 2–17 (OMOP CDM, obesity SNOMED hierarchy).

### Most common co-occurring mental health diagnoses (% of the obese-child cohort)

| Diagnosis category | Patients | % of cohort |
|---|---|---|
| Anxiety disorders | 5,554 | 14.2% |
| Depressive disorders | 4,131 | 10.6% |
| ADHD | 3,210 | 8.2% |
| Trauma/stress-related (PTSD, acute stress, adjustment) | 3,047 | 7.8% |
| Autism spectrum disorder | 2,345 | 6.0% |
| Disruptive/conduct disorders | 1,844 | 4.7% |
| Eating disorders | 1,327 | 3.4% |

### Diagnoses that most often co-occur *with each other* (top pairs)

| Pair | Patients with both | % of cohort |
|---|---|---|
| Anxiety + Depression | 2,396 | 6.1% |
| Anxiety + Trauma/stress | 2,257 | 5.8% |
| ADHD + Anxiety | 1,217 | 3.1% |
| Depression + Trauma/stress | 1,175 | 3.0% |
| ADHD + Depression | 848 | 2.2% |
| ADHD + ASD | 665 | 1.7% |
| Anxiety + Eating disorder | 632 | 1.6% |

The dominant cluster is **internalizing (anxiety–depression–trauma)**, with ADHD and ASD forming a secondary neurodevelopmental cluster.

*Caveat:* these are diagnosis-code co-occurrence prevalences in one EHR, not causal or incidence estimates; ascertainment (kids in care get more codes of all kinds) inflates co-occurrence.

## Plausible appetite/stress pathways linking them

These are mechanistic hypotheses from the literature, not derived from the EHR:

- **HPA axis / cortisol (the strongest bridge).** Chronic anxiety, depression, and trauma dysregulate the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis → sustained cortisol → visceral adiposity, insulin resistance, and increased intake of energy-dense "comfort" food. This is the most parsimonious link for the internalizing cluster above.
- **Reward/dopamine & emotional eating.** Depression and trauma alter mesolimbic dopamine reward signaling; hyperpalatable food becomes a self-soothing behavior. Overlaps with ADHD, where impaired dopaminergic inhibitory control drives impulsive/dysregulated eating.
- **Leptin–insulin CNS resistance.** Obesity-related leptin/insulin resistance impairs hypothalamic satiety and also affects hippocampal/limbic circuits implicated in mood — a bidirectional loop.
- **Serotonin & the gut–brain axis.** Serotonergic tone governs both satiety and mood; diet-driven microbiome shifts and low-grade inflammation feed back on both.
- **Neuroinflammation.** Adipose-derived cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, CRP) cross into the CNS and are associated with depressive symptoms — a shared inflammatory substrate.
- **Sleep disruption.** Obesity (OSA) and anxiety/depression both fragment sleep, dysregulating ghrelin/leptin (↑hunger) and worsening mood — a reinforcing triangle.
- **Medication iatrogenesis.** Some psychotropics used for these very diagnoses (certain antipsychotics, some antidepressants) drive appetite and weight gain, confounding the association.
